multilingual-field: Use name to submit translations as title[de], title[fr], title[it] and title[rm]. includeEnglish adds English. Select variant=textarea for long copy or layout=columns to compare translations. Copy fills an empty language from sourceLanguage.
uid-input: Collect a CHE business identifier with its modulo-11 check digit. A valid entry is grouped on blur. Pass validationMessage to localize the native validation error.
iban-input: Use for Swiss and Liechtenstein accounts. Valid accounts are grouped on blur. Use isSwissIban and compactIban on submitted values.
ahv-input: Accept 13 digits beginning with 756. The component validates the EAN‑13 check digit and groups a valid number on blur. Pass validationMessage to localize native form errors.
phone-input: Accept ordinary nine-digit Swiss national numbers, domestic trunk prefixes and international +41 or 0041 input. Format valid entries on blur. Short service codes use a separate field.
swiss-qr-bill: Supply a structured creditor address, a Swiss or Liechtenstein IBAN and a compatible reference. Use printSwissQrBill with the component ref to print one payment slip on A4 at actual size.
grid-overlay: Mount the overlay alongside a page or inside a positioned container with placement set to container. Use hidden to toggle it. The portal shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+G.
accordion: Use a question or section name as each trigger. The full header is clickable, long labels wrap, and arrow keys move between headers without opening them.
alert: Choose a heading level that fits the surrounding page. Reserve a live announcement for information that appears after an action. The visible symbol and text also communicate the tone.
alert-dialog: Give the confirmation a specific action label. Initial focus goes to Cancel. Clicking the backdrop leaves the decision open.
app-shell: On small screens, Escape closes the open index when focus is inside the shell and returns focus to its trigger. Toolbar controls wrap as labels grow.
aspect-ratio: Use fit="contain" for a screenshot or diagram whose edges must remain visible. The default cover fit fills the frame by cropping when needed.
attachment: Use the file name as the link and include size or format alongside it. The name can wrap and is isolated from metadata written in another direction.
avatar: Provide the person’s name even when supplying a photo. If the image fails, initials include complete accented letters where the browser supports grapheme segmentation.
badge: Use a short status name. The mark stays with the start of a wrapped label, and its shape remains distinct in forced colors.
breadcrumb: Give the trail a navigation label and identify the current page. The separator follows the writing direction, including when a long link wraps.
bubble: Put a message in the start or end position to distinguish speakers. Long words wrap inside the available width, including in right-to-left conversations.
button: Give the action a verb. A busy button keeps its label visible and disables repeat activation while the action is pending.
button-group: Give related actions a group name. Keep them in task order so keyboard users reach them in the same sequence in a narrow layout.
calendar: Pass canton to mark public holidays in the grid and list their names below the month. Add holidayRegion for a local schedule. Arrow keys move the active day.
canton-combobox: Type a canton name in the active language. Alt+Down opens suggestions and Alt+Up dismisses them while preserving the committed canton.
canton-select: Set order="name" to sort the cantons in the current language. The submitted abbreviation stays the same. The default order follows federal statistics.
card: Keep the heading, content and actions for one object together. Footers align at the base of stretched cards and the padding adapts to narrow pages.
carousel: Start a swipe on slide content to navigate. Gestures that start on a nested control belong to that control. A single slide adds no carousel tab stop.
chart: Include readable category names and values in the accompanying table. Visitors can compare signed values or read a long category name without interpreting bar length.
checkbox: Set indeterminate for a partially selected set. Clear that prop when the user chooses a definite checked or unchecked value.
code-block: If automatic copying is unavailable, the control selects the code and focuses it. Use the browser’s copy command while the selection is active.
collapsible: Write a summary that identifies the content behind it. The native disclosure works with Enter or Space and gives touch users a full row to press.
combobox: Provide a clearLabel to let visitors remove a committed choice and return to search. A required field can display an inline message until a valid option is chosen.
command: Label each command by its action. Moving the pointer changes the active result while keyboard focus stays in the search field.
context-menu: The invoking region identifies the open menu through aria-controls. The menu uses visible-viewport positioning and restores focus to the invocation point.
currency-chf: Pass the unformatted amount and a Swiss locale. The data element keeps the raw value and isolates the formatted currency from surrounding right-to-left text.
data-table: Compare underlying values when sorting formatted cells. Column headers expose the sort direction and act as full-cell buttons. Translate sortHint when the surrounding interface changes language.
date-picker: Pass canton and an optional holidayRegion to highlight holidays in the dialog. All dates within min and max remain selectable. The clear action updates the submitted value and restores trigger focus.
description-list: Use one distinct term per value. Narrow summaries stack each term above its detail. Wider containers align terms and values in two columns.
dialog: Name the dialog and provide an explicit close action. Opening locks background scrolling. Escape closes it and restores focus to its trigger.
direction: Set dir on the smallest region that changes writing direction. Logical alignment then follows the text direction in nested navigation and messages.
drawer: The bottom drawer locks background scrolling while open, with a neutral scrim and a swipe handle separate from the scrollable content.
dropdown-menu: Keep item labels actionable. Use shortcut to show a keyboard binding that the application already implements. The popup follows the visible viewport when zoom or scrolling changes it.
empty: Explain why the view is empty and offer a recovery action, such as clearing a filter. Set the heading level to fit the page.
field: Put the label, help and correction next to their control. The accessible description reads the error first and includes each referenced hint only once.
figure: Supply meaningful alternative text for informative images. The caption can identify the study and credit can link to its source. The image keeps its intrinsic proportions.
grid: Use width="site" for a centered 100rem frame. Column spans follow the container width. Use fields with rows to compose rectangular areas, or select thirds or five-seven for lead/detail pairs. Give each GridItem a field name and use subgrid="rows" to align content across cards.
hover-card: Touch users get a taller trigger. Long panel text wraps and the panel fits the visible viewport while remaining reachable by keyboard.
icon: Use a decorative icon beside visible action text. Give an icon-only button or link its own accessible name. Set the icon’s label when the graphic itself conveys meaning.
input: Use readOnly when a value is available to inspect or copy. Validation marks the logical leading edge of the control, including in right-to-left layouts.
input-group: Use an affix for a unit or prefix that belongs to the input. The group shares a visible focus and validation boundary, and long affixes can wrap.
input-otp: Formatted-paste handling respects read-only and disabled fields. Editable inputs retain leading zeros and normalize full-width digits.
item: Place the primary record name in the title and secondary actions at the trailing edge. Long identifiers reflow inside the row.
kbd: Use short key names for most shortcuts. Longer translated names can wrap inside a narrow column without clipping.
label: Connect the label to its input with htmlFor and id. Activating the label focuses or activates the associated native control.
locale-select: An empty language list disables the selector. Available languages retain caller-defined order, endonyms and language attributes.
marker: Pair the symbol with a status name. Its shape remains recognizable even when a translated label wraps over multiple lines.
menubar: Coarse pointers get taller top-level actions. Menus accept shortcut hints, and horizontal arrow navigation transfers focus between groups.
message: Supply a readable author and a machine-readable timestamp. The author name is isolated from surrounding bidirectional message text.
message-scroller: If the viewport grows or content shrinks until the latest message is visible, the log resumes following and removes the redundant jump button.
native-select: The line variant marks a disabled field with a dashed underline. Native selection, multiple values, reset and validation remain available.
navigation-menu: Label the navigation and mark the current link. In touch layouts each link gets a 44px target and its padding follows the writing direction.
pagination: Supply a localized page-name formatter for number-only links. An explicit accessible name takes precedence. Mark the current page so it can be identified without color.
popover: The panel wraps long content and follows the visible viewport during zoom or resize. Escape restores trigger focus and outside clicks preserve the destination.
progress: Pass a value for measurable progress or omit it while the total is unknown. The indeterminate track stays visible with reduced motion.
prose: Use semantic headings, paragraphs, figures and links inside the reading column. Media scales to the column and quotation rules follow the writing direction.
questionnaire: An empty questionnaire can display a localized message. If a previous answer becomes unavailable before submission, the user returns to that question with the other answers intact.
radio-group: Use a group label for a choice with one answer. Passing form associates each radio with that form even when the fieldset sits outside it.
resizable: The resize handle expands to 44 CSS pixels at the default root size on coarse pointers. Keyboard arrows adjust the split and Enter restores the previous size.
scroll-area: Name a scrollable region so keyboard users can identify it. Horizontal overflow stays inside the region while vertical scrolling can continue on the page.
select: Use native selection for a short, familiar set of options. The validation rule follows the logical start of the control in either writing direction.
separator: Decorative separators stay hidden from assistive technology. Expose a semantic separator and orientation when the boundary conveys structure.
sheet: Place related editing controls inside the panel and name it. The sheet body scrolls independently while keyboard focus remains inside the open modal.
sidebar: Keep navigation labels meaningful on their own. The scrollable index leaves space around focused entries, and long masthead or footer text can wrap.
skeleton: Reserve the expected space while content loads. The placeholder stays silent for assistive technology and the animation stops under reduced motion.
slider: Set min, max and step to meaningful values, and supply a label. Native arrow-key input then moves the value by the configured step.
spinner: Give the spinner a label when it conveys loading status. An unlabelled spinner is decorative. Its animation stops under reduced motion.
stack: Use inset for padding in multiples of the spacing unit. The ink and paper surfaces establish matching themes for the controls they contain.
steps: Give the sequence a name and pass a stable current step ID. The ordered list exposes the active step to assistive technology. In narrow layouts the steps run vertically.
swiss-address-form: Enter 6900 to choose Lugano, Massagno or Paradiso from the local postcode directory. Accepting a suggestion sets both locality and canton. You can also enter both manually.
swiss-date: Pass a civil date for a specific calendar day. The time element keeps its machine-readable value and isolates the localized date in bidirectional text.
swiss-postal-code-input: A full-field paste accepts four digits, full-width digits or a CH-prefixed postal code. The submitted four-digit value preserves leading zeros.
switch: Use a switch for an immediate on/off setting. Keep its label meaningful in both states. Long state text wraps while the control keeps its shape.
table: Mark amount cells numeric to align comparable values. Ordinary franc amounts stay together and exceptionally long numbers can wrap inside the table.
tabs: Use automatic activation for immediate panels or manual activation when opening a panel is costly. Vertical tab labels wrap within a capped column.
text-link: Use the action variant for a prominent navigation link. Inline focus rings follow the foreground color, including on inverse surfaces.
textarea: Set rows for the starting height and enable auto-grow when appropriate. Read-only and validation states follow the same conventions as Input.
toast: A focused notification can be dismissed with Escape. Its dismiss button and Escape return focus to the control used to reach this notification.
toggle: Keep the toggle’s label stable and communicate its on/off state with aria-pressed. The control supports Space and long labels can wrap.
toggle-group: Tab enters a group once. Arrow keys move focus, Home and End reach its edges, and pressing Space changes the focused option. Use layout="grid" for equal-width tiles with arrow navigation between rows.
tooltip: Attach a short description to an existing focusable control. Focus shows it immediately. Escape dismisses it and the popup stays within the visible viewport.
trace: Time and event text align to a consistent gutter. Long entries wrap, keyboard focus outlines the disclosure, and touch users get a taller summary.
typography: Choose the semantic heading level with as and its visual size with variant. The title role scales with the container and wraps long multilingual headings.
bar-chart: Compare signed values on a common scale with directly labelled bars. Pass title, description and data with label and value for each observation. Use loading while fetching data and formatValue for units.
line-chart: Plot an ordered series with a labelled scale and a readable data table. Pass title, description and data with label and value for each observation. Use loading while fetching data and formatValue for units.
sparkline: Show a short trend with its last observation and the underlying values. Pass title, description and data with label and value for each observation. Use loading while fetching data and formatValue for units.
chart-table: Compare magnitudes while reading precise values in a semantic table. Pass title, description and data with label and value for each observation. Use loading while fetching data and formatValue for units.
